versions.versionTitle: Mishnah Torah, Yod ha-hazakah, trans. by Simon Glazer, 1927
versions.text: A disciple of the wise shall not walk about with his head high up in the air and neck stretched out, the subject of which was denounced, saying: "And they walk with stretched necks and wanton eyes" (Is. 3.16); nor overslow as bringing heel to toe like some women and the arrogant, the subject of which was denounced, saying: "Walking and measuring as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet" (Ibid.); nor run about after the fashion of the mad, nor bent as if hunch-backed, but looking downward as if in praying position, and as if occupied and going on some errand of business. Even from the way a person walks it is apparent whether he is wise and sensible or foolish and imprudent. For even so did Solomon in his wisdom say: "Yea also, when a fool walketh by the way, his understanding faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool" (Ecc. 10.3), meaning that he himself proclaims to everybody that he is a fool.11Berakot, 43b. C.
